Briefly stated the facts of the cases as emerged from DARs are that on 20.05.2021 at about 04:00
p.m., the deceased Akil Ahamad was standing on the road side near Rishab Vihar Chowk,
Delhi-110092, all of a sudden, one grey black car bearing registration no. Dl5Cp-6969 (in short
'offending vehicle'), being driven by the respondent no.1 namely Anmol Chopra came at a fast speed
and in a rash and negligent manner and hit another car bearing no. Dl7Cr-6760 driven by one lady
namely Dr. Ayesha Parveen (injured in Mact no.30/22) and then hit the fruit cart of deceased
namely Bablu @ Akil Ahamad and thereafter, hit the traffic signal light pole and stopped.

The
impact of the collision threw off the deceased Bablu @ Akil Ahamad about 5 feet from the accident
spot.
One person namely Sanu dialed at 100 number.

Police came at the spot and injured Ayesha
Parveen was taken to Pushpanjali Medical Centre, Vikas Marg, Delhi, where her Mlc was prepared
and was discharged on the next date.

The injured Akil Ahamad was removed to Dr. Hedgewar
Hospital, Delhi, where his Mlc was prepared and thereafter, he was shifted to Dr. R.M.L. Hospital,
New Delhi, where he died during treatment on 22.02.2021.

In connection with the accident, initially
the case was registered vide Fir no.118/21, under sections 279/337 Ipc, Ps Anand Vihar, Delhi and
after death of Akil Ahamad, sections 304-A Ipc was added to the case.

After completion of the
investigation, respondent no.1 was charge-sheeted for offences under sections 279/337/304-A Ipc
and DARs for compensation to the claimants were filed before this Tribunal by the Investigating
Agency.

As per DARs, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending
vehicle by respondent no.1, which was owned by respondent no.2 and insured with respondent no.3
at the time of accident.

ISSUE NO.1 (in both cases):
10. Issue no.1, being interlinked in both the cases, shall be decided here together by my common findings.
It is the settled proposition of law that in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.

However,
the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.

Strict rules of evidence are not applicable ________________________________________________________________________________ MACT nos.31/22 & 30/22 7 of 26 Pages in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others.,
MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand & Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 &

The impact of the collision was so strong which resulted into throwing off the deceased Bablu @ Akil Ahamad about 5 feet from the place of impact.

PW2 further deposed that thereafter, he dialed at 100 number and after 10 minutes, the PCR van came on the spot, meanwhile,
he caught the driver Anmol Chopra till police personnel came there.

After that, he followed the police personnel, who brought the Bablu @ Akil Ahamad and driver of the offending vehicle i.e.

As per the version of PW2, death of deceased was caused due to the forceful impact of the accident.

ISSUE NO.2 17. In view of the finding on issue no.1, it is held that petitioners in both the cases are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v. Willoughby (1970) AC 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).

COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION (In re: deceased Akil Ahamad)
18.
The present case pertains to the death of deceased Akil Ahamad.

In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.

sentences.text: Further, the guidelines have been reiterated by the Constitution Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court in a case titled as National Insurance Company vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.

sentences.text:
Decided on 31.10.2017,
laying down the general principles for computation of compensation in death cases.

The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"18.
If these determinations are standardized, there will be uniformity and consistency in the decisions.
There will be lesser need for detailed evidence.
It will also be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
Step-3 (Actual Calculation)

The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the legal heirs of the deceased.
The funeral expenses, cost of transportation of the body (if incurred) and the cost of any medical treatment of the deceased before death (if incurred) should also be added."

The relevant extract is as under:
"Broadly speaking while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages.

Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred and which is capable of being calculated in terms of money-, whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

In order to appreciate two concepts pecuniary damages may, include expenses incurred by the claimant: (i) medical attendance; (ii) loss of earning of profit upto the date of trial; (iii) other material loss.

So far non- pecuniary damages are concerned,
they may include (i) damages for mental and physical shock, pain suffering, already suffered or likely to be suffered in future; (ii) damages to compensate for the loss of amenities of life which may include a variety of matters i.e. on account of injury the claimant may not be able to walk, run or sit;
(iii) damages for the loss of expectation of life, i.e. on account of injury the normal longevity of the person concerned is shortened; (iv) inconvenience, discomfort,
disappointment, hardship, frustration and mental stress in life."
29. Further, in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases.

Non-Pecuniary Damages (general damages)
(iv) Damages to pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage)

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is the settled proposition of law that in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However,
the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others.,
MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand & Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 &
Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.
11.
Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by him in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. v.
Kamlesh, 2009(3) AD (Delhi) 310.
13.
Not only this, the respondent no.1 has been charge-sheeted under Sections 279/337/304-A IPC in the criminal case by the police after detailed investigation and in a motor vehicle accident claim case, the contents of charge-sheet are admissible in evidence and deemed to be correct under Rule 7 of Delhi Motor Accident Tribunal Rules, 2008, which support the version of petitioners regarding rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1.
14.
In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.
Further, the guidelines have been reiterated by the Constitution Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court in a case titled as National Insurance Company vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.
To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
It is evident that Aadhaar Card and Election Identity Card of the deceased (Ex.PW3/1) shows his residential address of Delhi.
Therefore, in absence of anPECUNIy documentary evidence in respect of education, income and occupation of deceased, his income has to be assessed at par with minimum wages applicable to unskilled category of workers in the State of Delhi on the date of accident (20.05.2021), which were Rs.15,908/- per month.
Thus, the income of deceased is considered to be Rs.15,908/- per month.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The deceased can be considered to be a self-employed.
After choosing the age, multiplier and income of the deceased, necessary deductions have to be made out of the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses.

The petitioner(s) in both the cases shall open saving bank account near the place of their residence.
Further, the bank(s) of petitioner is/ are directed to comply with the following conditions:-
(a) The Bank shall not permit any joint name(s) to be added in the savings bank account or fixed deposit accounts of the claimant(s) i.e., the savings bank account(s)

However,
the statement containing FDR number, FDR amount, date of maturity and maturity amount shall be furnished by bank to the claimant(s).
(c) The monthly interest be credited by Electronic Clearing System (ECS) in the savings bank account of the claimant(s) near the place of their residence.
(d) The maturity amounts of the FDR(s) be credited by Electronic Clearing System (ECS) in the savings bank account of the claimant(s) near the place of their residence.
(e) No loan, advance, withdrawal or pre-mature discharge be allowed on the fixed deposits without permission of the Court.
(f) The concerned bank shall not issue any cheque book and/or debit card to claimant(s).
